section_summary: The section begins with the end of a Japanese plan for North Pacific fishing and then follows Allied correspondence about a Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition: objections, inspectors, its route, passage through Lombok Strait, and the flag its vessels should fly. A Tokyo despatch encloses weekly coastal whaling and fleet preparation reports. The section also contains a short exchange about Japanese cultured pearl exports and one later, 1948 aide-mémoire concerning another Antarctic expedition.

subfiles.title: Japanese plan for North Pacific fishing
subfiles.about: Proposes crab and salmon canneries, trawling, and whaling in northern waters.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages specify grounds, seasons, vessels, crews, materials, and estimated output for crab and salmon floating canneries, trawling, and Kuril Islands whaling. They cite prewar Japanese fishing and anticipated postwar resources.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section referral of Japanese northern fishing request
subfiles.about: Refers the Japanese request for possible Soviet consultation.
subfiles.summary: Notes likely United States opposition to Japanese fishing near the Aleutians and in the Bering Sea.

subfiles.title: Delay Soviet presentation of Japanese fishing request
subfiles.about: Advises delaying presentation of the northern fishing request to Soviet representatives.
subfiles.summary: The Department awaits Far Eastern Commission consideration of fishing and whaling policy.

subfiles.title: British position on Antarctic whaling and inspectors
subfiles.about: Withdraws British objections and offers two inspectors, subject to arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Britain seeks cancellation of the August tanker-conversion directive, reimbursement of inspector expenses from voyage proceeds, rations, and prompt reporting instructions.

subfiles.title: Reply to British Embassy on tanker conversion and expedition route
subfiles.about: Reports suspension of tanker conversion and supplies fleet sailing and route details.
subfiles.summary: The Department says conversion of a tanker for Bonin Islands whaling will stop. It lists departures from Yokosuka and Nagasaki, the route through Lombok Strait, offshore limits, and expected travel time.

subfiles.title: Norwegian objections to Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Recounts Knut Lykke's objections and proposed Norwegian alternative.
subfiles.summary: Lykke sought rescission or a Norwegian-run expedition; Acheson promised an inquiry.

subfiles.title: British inspector terms sent to SCAP
subfiles.about: Conveys British inspector proposals and asks SCAP to consider rations.
subfiles.summary: Britain offers two inspectors and seeks rations, expense reimbursement, and reporting instructions. The Department urges an exception to the ration rule and requests SCAP's comments.

subfiles.title: Request for Norwegian reasons opposing whaling
subfiles.about: Requests the full grounds for Norway's protest.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo's files lack details of the Norwegian objections cited in a September note.

subfiles.title: London inquiry about whaling conference papers
subfiles.about: Asks when draft agenda and rules will arrive.
subfiles.summary: The British delegation needs the papers before departing on November 10.

subfiles.title: Outgoing telegram draft
subfiles.about: A largely illegible draft follows the London conference inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR does not establish its substantive message.

subfiles.title: Outgoing telegram
subfiles.about: An outgoing telegram is too damaged in OCR to identify its subject securely.
subfiles.summary: Only the form and Acheson signature are clear.

subfiles.title: British inspectors' travel difficulty
subfiles.about: Asks how late-arriving British inspectors could join the expedition.
subfiles.summary: They cannot reach Hong Kong before November 21; Britain does not seek a sailing delay.

subfiles.title: Alternative inspector rendezvous
subfiles.about: Seeks SCAP's views on British and Norwegian inspectors joining later.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks whether British inspectors could board near Lombok Strait and a Norwegian inspector could briefly visit a Japanese factory ship in Antarctic waters.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on Allied inspector support
subfiles.about: Addresses rations and expense arrangements for Allied whaling inspectors.
subfiles.summary: The OCR is badly damaged, but discusses reporting dates, rations, salaries, and reimbursement.

subfiles.title: Proposed Norwegian inspector Harald Ostby
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP's response to Norway's proposal to send Ostby.
subfiles.summary: Norway requests rations and reimbursement; Ostby's credentials and November reporting deadline are relayed.

subfiles.title: Request for passage through Lombok Strait
subfiles.about: Seeks Dutch agreement for the Japanese fleet's direct passage.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo describes the longer alternative route, navigational hazards, extra fuel, and urgent sailing date.

subfiles.title: British inspector salary rate
subfiles.about: Supplies the British inspectors' monthly salary rate.
subfiles.summary: The stated rate excludes food and accommodation.

subfiles.title: Dutch clearance requested for Lombok Strait
subfiles.about: Requests Dutch approval of the fleet's passage through Lombok Strait.
subfiles.summary: The Department relays Tokyo's navigation and fuel arguments and asks the embassy to cable Tokyo directly if the Netherlands agrees.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hague approach
subfiles.about: Advises that the Lombok passage request has gone to The Hague.
subfiles.summary: The embassy is to raise it with the Dutch Government and answer Tokyo directly.

subfiles.title: Flag for the Japanese whaling fleet
subfiles.about: Seeks urgent decision on the fleet's flag.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo says existing SCAJAP flags have restricted uses and proposes a reversed-color Japanese flag if acceptable.

subfiles.title: Conversation on SCAP flags
subfiles.about: Reviews available flags and possible extension to whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: Navy and State officials examine flags used by repatriation ships. They consider extending an existing SCAJAP flag simpler than promulgating a new reverse-color ensign.

subfiles.title: Preliminary flag recommendation
subfiles.about: Favors extending an existing SCAJAP flag to the expedition.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Tokyo's preference before acting.

subfiles.title: New Zealand covering letter
subfiles.about: Encloses New Zealand's aide-mémoire on Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Powles expects an early decision on appointing a New Zealand inspector.

subfiles.title: New Zealand views on the proposed expedition
subfiles.about: Withdraws objections while seeking safeguards and future consultation.
subfiles.summary: New Zealand asks about the route and fuel, welcomes inspection, and seeks cancellation of the tanker-conversion directive.

subfiles.title: Reply to New Zealand on conversion and route
subfiles.about: Reports suspended tanker conversion and the expedition's sailing details.
subfiles.summary: The Department says conversion will stop pending a decision on the vessel's future. It gives departures, ships, the course through Lombok Strait, offshore restrictions, and estimated travel time.

subfiles.title: Third Antarctic expedition response
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP's decision to authorize a third expedition without a third factory ship.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites Japan's food and foreign exchange needs, SCAP's authority, and New Zealand's lack of objection to that year's expedition. It suggests route inquiries go directly to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Text of New Zealand note forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards New Zealand's October 29 position on the Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: The quoted note withdraws objections while raising consultation, route, inspection, security, and tanker-conversion concerns.

subfiles.title: Preliminary Dutch response on Lombok Strait
subfiles.about: Reports Dutch Navy approval conditional on continuous passage.
subfiles.summary: The Netherlands Indies Government still must confirm; an objection remains possible.

subfiles.title: Expedite final Lombok clearance
subfiles.about: Requests urgent follow-up on Dutch permission.
subfiles.summary: The fleet expects to reach Lombok around November 23.

subfiles.title: Norwegian response to Antarctic whaling authorization
subfiles.about: Acquiesces in the expedition but maintains objections and proposes an inspector.
subfiles.summary: Norway opposes a third factory ship and future Japanese expeditions. It offers Lieutenant Commander Harald Ostby as inspector and seeks subsistence and reimbursement.

subfiles.title: Reply to Norwegian ambassador
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains the halted tanker conversion and provides fleet route details.
subfiles.summary: The letter reports that Bonin Islands use of the tanker is impracticable, so conversion will stop. It then gives ship departures, the Lombok route, coastal limits, and timing.

subfiles.title: SCAP response on Norwegian inspector
subfiles.about: Clears Ostby conditionally but rejects payment from voyage proceeds.
subfiles.summary: SCAP offers rations on a dollar-reimbursement basis and requires Ostby to report by November 8.

subfiles.title: Weekly report on Japanese whaling activities
subfiles.about: Transmits seven coastal whaling and Antarctic fleet reports.
subfiles.summary: The enclosures cover September 22 through October 12, 1946.

subfiles.title: Coastal whaling report, September 22–28
subfiles.about: Records catches, inactive vessels, and new construction.
subfiles.summary: Japanese stations and catchers took 55 whales. The report lists boats in repair and progress on catchers and a factory ship.

subfiles.title: Coastal whaling report, September 29–October 5
subfiles.about: Updates catches, station assignments, repairs, and construction.
subfiles.summary: The report totals 67 whales, notes closure of the Okochi station, and updates catcher and factory-ship work.

subfiles.title: Coastal whaling report, October 6–12
subfiles.about: Records the week's catches and vessel construction status.
subfiles.summary: The report totals 56 whales and lists three inactive catchers and construction progress.

subfiles.title: Whale products from Japanese coastal whaling
subfiles.about: Tabulates whale products for three weekly periods.
subfiles.summary: Company totals cover oil, meat, blubber, leather material, and other products.

subfiles.title: Antarctic fleet status, September 22–28
subfiles.about: Tracks conversion and repair of the 1946–47 Antarctic fleet.
subfiles.summary: The tables cover factory ships, carriers, tankers, and catchers, with locations and estimated completion dates.

subfiles.title: Antarctic fleet status, September 29–October 5
subfiles.about: Updates preparation of the Japanese Antarctic fleet.
subfiles.summary: Conversion of the principal factory ships and carriers advanced while catcher repairs and construction continued.

subfiles.title: Antarctic fleet status, October 6–12
subfiles.about: Reports further vessel preparation before departure.
subfiles.summary: The tables show near-complete conversion of major ships and progress on catcher repairs and construction.

subfiles.title: Routing note on pearl-industry inquiry
subfiles.about: Suggests withholding a pearl-industry cable because SCAP has answered.
subfiles.summary: Asks Claxton to handle the Civil Affairs Division letter.

subfiles.title: War Department reply on Japanese pearls
subfiles.about: Relays SCAP's estimate for pearl exports and returns a draft cable.
subfiles.summary: SCAP expects old-stock shipments beginning in early 1947 and new stocks only late that year.

subfiles.title: Earlier War Department reply on Japanese pearls
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP's pearl-export answer from an October teleconference.
subfiles.summary: It recommends against dispatching the proposed cable.

subfiles.title: Cultured pearls memorandum
subfiles.about: Requests advice on pearl stocks and export timing.
subfiles.summary: Reports possible stock buildup in Japanese post exchanges.

subfiles.title: Proposed pearl-industry inquiry to SCAP
subfiles.from: War Department and Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks about Japanese pearl stocks and the start of exports.
subfiles.summary: Cites information from Goldstone of the Imperial Pearl Syndicate.

subfiles.title: SCAP response on inspectors boarding en route
subfiles.about: Allows a possible British boarding at Lombok and a brief Norwegian Antarctic visit.
subfiles.summary: British arrangements must not delay the fleet and require prompt confirmation, supplies, and dollar reimbursement.

subfiles.title: British inspector travel plan sent to SCAP
subfiles.about: Says one British inspector can reach Surabaya by November 21.
subfiles.summary: Requests rations and confirmation of the fleet's route and Lombok arrival date.

subfiles.title: British commitment to repay ration costs
subfiles.about: Agrees to dollar reimbursement for the inspector's rations.
subfiles.summary: The commitment depends on a reasonable chance of joining the fleet en route.

subfiles.title: British plan for one inspector at Surabaya
subfiles.about: Plans to fly one inspector to Surabaya and seeks boarding details.
subfiles.summary: Britain cannot send a second inspector; its consul seeks Dutch landing and rendezvous arrangements.

subfiles.title: Tokyo request for flag decision
subfiles.about: Urgently seeks instructions on the flag for Japanese whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: Damaged OCR indicates concern about international recognition of merchant marine and modified code flags.

subfiles.title: Authorization of SCAJAP flag E
subfiles.about: Authorizes the merchant ensign with modified international code flag E.
subfiles.summary: The Department will notify other countries; SCAP should promulgate the arrangement locally.
